pageText: Detect inconsistency between direct and indirect evidence in network meta-analysis. Performs node-splitting (Dias et al. 2010) on every comparison with a closed loop, and a global design-by-treatment test (Higgins et al. 2012). Multi-arm studies are supported when all their pairwise contrasts are entered.
A, B, effect, SE[, study ID]

One row per two-arm study; multiple rows per comparison allowed. A multi-arm study needs a study ID and all k(k−1)/2 of its pairwise contrasts, consistent with one set of arm estimates to within netmeta's tolerance (0.001); incomplete or inconsistent multi-arm studies and repeated two-arm study IDs are refused.
RE models estimate shared τ² from consistency-model residuals before testing inconsistency — addresses the "FE Q-statistics inflated under heterogeneity" caveat below.
Import the shared ma-comparisons-v1 network (arm-level events/n), converted to contrast log-OR/RR for this app.

direct and indirect whiskers should overlap for a consistent network. Non-overlapping whiskers with |z| > 1.96 indicate a specific loop with inconsistency. The global design-by-treatment test is the omnibus check.

For independent two-arm studies, removing each direct comparison gives the same split as netmeta back-calculation / SIDE at a fixed shared τ².
